newsitem.title: USA: NASD to restructure board, speed decision-making.
newsitem.headline: NASD to restructure board, speed decision-making.

text.p: The National Association of Securities Dealers said Thursday its board has approved a plan designed to speed decision-making on issues affecting listed securities and discipline among brokers.
The plan calls for an interlocking board structure, with both the Nasdaq and NASD Regulation boards shrinking in size and becoming part of an expanded NASD parent board, it said.
NASD Chairman Frank Zarb said the proposed changes "will enhance the core corporate governance principles put in place last year by creating a more efficient structure."

The changes are the first major overhaul of NASD and its units at the top since the securities industry's self-regulatory organisation adopted far-reaching recommendations by an independent panel led by former New Hampshire Senator Warren Rudman in September 1995.

Zarb said the plan "maintains the spirit and principles" of the Rudman panel's recommendations, which came amid criticism over NASD's laxity in regulating Nasdaq dealers. Those recommendations resulted in the creation of separate units to run the Nasdaq and regulate the brokerage industry, with NASD serving as parent corporation.

As an example of how fast decisions can be made under the proposed structure, he noted that actions by the Nasdaq and NASD Regulation boards could be taken up the next day by the parent board. In the current system final decisions could take 60 days.
Zarb said Rudman was consulted about the plan and was "satisfied" with it.
A single NASD board executive committee will be created to replace the two subsidiary executive committees.
A 12-member National Adjudicatory Council will replace the National Business Conduct Committee and will review decisions such as disciplinary orders.

Under the plan, the total number of directors will be reduced to 17 from 48. Board committees will also be cut to five from nine, and board meetings will be less frequent -- seven instead of 17 annually.
The proposed changes are subject to approval by NASD members and the Securities and Exchange Commission, which has oversight powers over the self-regulatory organisation.
The NASD said its board will maintain a majority of non-industry or independent members, while the two subsidiary boards will be balanced between industry and non-industry representatives.

The NASD board, currently with 10 directors, will increase to 27 members. Its non-industry or independent majority will include at least four public governors, a representative from the Nasdaq-listed companies and a representative each from the mutual fund and insurance industries.
NASD said its board will retain ultimate policymaking, oversight and corporate authority as the parent holding company.
Brokerage regulator NASD Regulation's board, which currently has 24 members, will have five to eight members, with each serving a three-year term.
The board will remain primarily responsible for all brokerage industry regulatory matters, but it may take decisions directly to the parent board.

The Nasdaq, with 16 members currently, will also shrink to between five and eight members. It will retain primary authority for market-related rulemaking. Rule changes it makes on such matters as fees or other charges will be subject to approval by the parent board.
